issue.title: Support root dotnet-tools.json
issue.problem: Arcade dependency updates and codeflow currently recognize only .config/dotnet-tools.json. They must also support dotnet-tools.json at the repository root.

decisions.whenOneExists: Update or merge the existing manifest.
decisions.whenBothExist: Update and merge both manifests independently, without precedence.
decisions.dependencyScope: Only modify a manifest when it contains the dependency being updated or removed.
decisions.invalidJson: Preserve the existing failure behavior for malformed manifests.

reviewChunks.title: Support multiple manifests in dependency updates
reviewChunks.goal: Allow DependencyFileManager operations to discover and process either or both supported manifests.

work: Define constants for both supported manifest paths.
Remove the singular manifest read API; manifest discovery is an internal DependencyFileManager implementation detail.
Add separate private TryGet methods for the root and .config manifests.
Discover manifests at both supported paths.
Update, remove, and verify dependencies in every existing manifest.
Include the concrete manifest path in diagnostics.
Do not create a missing manifest.
Represent the root and .config manifests with separate properties.
Return every changed manifest from GetFilesToCommit.
Update build-update snapshots and change detection to account for multiple manifests.

tests: Neither manifest exists.
Only .config/dotnet-tools.json exists.
Only root dotnet-tools.json exists.
Both manifests exist.
A dependency exists in only one manifest.
A dependency exists in both manifests.
Unrelated tools remain unchanged.
Relative base paths are applied to both manifest paths.
Malformed JSON identifies the failing path.
Every changed manifest is committed exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria: Dependency updates, removals, and verification work at either location.
Both existing manifests are processed independently.
No manifest is created when neither exists.

reviewChunks.title: Support both manifests during codeflow
reviewChunks.goal: Exclude both manifests from ordinary patches and merge each one through the version-file conflict-resolution path.

work: Include both manifest paths in the codeflow dependency-file and patch-exclusion sets.
Three-way merge each supported manifest path independently.
Retain missing-file support for additions and deletions.
Three-way merge each supported manifest path independently.
Recognize conflicts at either path as version-file conflicts.
Treat both paths as dependency files rather than ordinary source changes.
Allow expected dependency-file divergence at either path.

tests: Forward flow with neither, either, and both manifests.
Backflow with neither, either, and both manifests.
Existence in any compared ref triggers merging for that path.
Additions and deletions use existing JSON merge semantics.
Root-manifest conflicts use version-file conflict handling.
Root-manifest dependency bumps are not classified as ordinary source changes.
Unrelated manifest edits remain meaningful changes.
Repositories using different locations on opposite sides do not implicitly delete either manifest.
acceptanceCriteria: Neither supported manifest is included in an ordinary codeflow patch.
Each existing manifest is independently merged in forward flow and backflow.
Root manifests participate in conflict resolution and change analysis like legacy manifests.
Existing legacy-path codeflow behavior remains unchanged.

reviewChunks.title: Add end-to-end codeflow coverage
reviewChunks.goal: Verify the behavior with real temporary Git repositories and complete forward-flow and backflow operations.

work: Add helpers for creating manifests at either or both supported paths.
Add focused forward-flow, backflow, concurrent-change, and location-migration scenarios.

tests: Root-only forward flow.
Root-only backflow.
Both manifests with a shared dependency.
A dependency present in only one manifest.
Migration from .config/dotnet-tools.json to root dotnet-tools.json.
Concurrent changes on both sides are merged rather than overwritten.
Neither manifest is staged through the ordinary patch path.
No duplicate staged paths or conflict markers remain.
acceptanceCriteria: Real Git codeflow tests pass for root-only, both-path, and migration scenarios.
DARC local forward-flow and backflow paths use the shared implementation.
Source-diff verification passes for legitimate dependency changes.

notes: The default verification excludes the slow codeflow test project, so it must be run explicitly for review chunks 2 and 3.
No Product Construction Service API contract or generated client change is expected.

risks.risk: Singular APIs and containers may cause one manifest to be dropped.
risks.mitigation: Keep the root and .config manifests explicit throughout discovery, mutation, commit generation, and change detection.

risks.risk: A root manifest may accidentally flow through the ordinary source patch.
risks.mitigation: Use the two centralized path constants consistently for exclusions, conflict recognition, analysis, and verification.

risks.risk: Location migration may be interpreted as cross-path semantic merging.
risks.mitigation: Treat each path independently; an explicit deletion and addition remain distinct file changes.

risks.risk: Processing both manifests could produce unstable commit ordering.
